finding.title: Harden or test the failure path of the unawaited CompletionDetectionService call in CompletionRepositoryImpl.markComplete
finding.rule: EH-2/EH-3 (errors converted/logged, no log-less catch) + Nygard (partial I/O failure) -- surfaced via this batch's tests

evidence.quote:
// Wait for any fire-and-forget unawaited futures to settle.
        await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);

finding.why: completion_detection_service.dart and learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart contain zero try/catch blocks (grep-confirmed), and the call site wraps them in unawaited(...) with no .catchError, so any exception during siyum detection (closed DB mid profile-switch, disk-full write, a malformed content lookup) becomes an unhandled Future error with no retry and no user-facing signal -- the completion itself still records, but the documented B1 policy ('a learner who bulk-marks a complete masechta still earns the siyum') silently fails to hold for that unit, permanently, with no reconciliation job anywhere in lib/ to catch the gap. No test anywhere in this batch makes checkAndRecordCompletions throw and asserts the outcome; the two tests that exercise this path can only prove the happy case, and both need a Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero) synchronization hack just to observe that -- itself a symptom that the design has no seam for verifying failure behavior deterministically.
finding.recommendation: Wrap the unawaited call in a .catchError (or add an internal try/catch inside checkAndRecordCompletions) that logs via AppLogger per EH-3; add a test that forces the detection service to throw (e.g. a ContentRepository stub that throws) and assert markComplete still returns successfully while the failure is logged.
acceptance_criteria: A test drives CompletionDetectionService.checkAndRecordCompletions to throw and asserts (a) markComplete still returns successfully and (b) AppLogger records the failure
The unawaited call site in completion_repository_impl.dart has a catch path instead of relying on the global zone error handler
